# Shadow

You might say
Add a light shadow under the card so it feels like it's floating above the page.

**Use light and depth to separate overlapping surfaces**·A shadow can show that a menu, dialog, or card sits above another surface. It should support a real layer relationship, not decorate every box. A small, consistent shadow scale is easier to read than many unrelated effects.

box-shadow

## You can say this to an AI Agent

> “
> Create a consistent shadow hierarchy: keep regular cards mostly flat, use light elevation for dropdowns and popovers, and a clearer but restrained modal shadow with one direction. Never shadow body text; test light and dark surfaces.

### When to use it

- Lift a floating menu above the page

→
- Separate a dialog from its backdrop
- Show an elevated card on a similar background

All states
All statesIn progressCompletedExpired
- Build a small set of depth levels

Inset shadows can make a surface appear recessed.

### When NOT to use it

- Add a strong shadow to every container
- Use several shadow directions on the same page
- Rely on shadow alone when contrast is too low
- Make a flat item look clickable when it is not

Body text with a drop shadow
